promise: Build a domain that still fits the rest of the application.
audience: Developers composing domain bundles into a Torque application.
trigger: Use when designing a Torque domain, authoring a bundle manifest and logic, wiring events/interfaces, or validating integration and schema changes.

modes.name: Place
modes.when: A domain boundary or dependency is unclear.
modes.output: A bundle responsibility map with declared interfaces, events, and optional dependencies.

modes.name: Author
modes.when: The domain contract and host are known.
modes.output: A manifest/logic/UI slice that fits the scoped data and coordinator contracts.

modes.name: Integrate
modes.when: A bundle must join a running app or evolve its data.
modes.output: A mount plan, integration checks, migration/rollback evidence, and explicit unknowns.

examples.title: A task bundle without a cross-domain table join
examples.brief: A fictional maintenance app needs task cards that react to asset changes.
examples.before: Import the asset bundle directly and query its tables from the task domain.
examples.after: Keep task storage scoped; declare the asset dependency and public query contract, subscribe to a past-tense asset event, and test missing optional dependencies.
examples.why: The useful boundary is the declared behavior and contract; a shared process does not justify shared private state.

marketing.headline: Add a domain without tangling the application.
marketing.lead: An authoring skill for Torque developers. Give a bundle a clear responsibility, connect it through declared interfaces and events, and plan data changes before they reach an existing store.

benefits.title: Keep domains independent
benefits.body: Own tables inside a bundle and call other domains through declared coordinator interfaces.

benefits.title: Make integration inspectable
benefits.body: Align manifest queries, routes, handlers, events and UI exports with the installed host contracts.

benefits.title: Treat data changes deliberately
benefits.body: Include migration, restart and rollback in the slice instead of assuming hot reload proves readiness.

walkthrough.title: Place the responsibility
walkthrough.detail: Inspect the current mount plan and neighboring bundles; decide whether configuration or a new domain is needed.

walkthrough.title: Author the contract
walkthrough.detail: Declare data ownership, named inputs, dependencies, events and degraded behavior.

walkthrough.title: Integrate on an isolated copy
walkthrough.detail: Exercise success, invalid input, authorization, missing dependencies, persistence and recovery.

use_when: A new domain must join an existing Torque app.
Two bundles are reaching into each other’s private tables.
A manifest or schema change needs a migration and rollback plan.
not_for: The Torque framework, its services or a replacement data layer.
A promise that historical package versions or private Git URLs are publicly available.
marketing.quickstart_prompt: Use Build with Torque to design a maintenance-task bundle. It should react to asset changes without reading another bundle’s private tables. Inspect this host first, then propose its manifest, public interfaces, events and migration checks.
marketing.output_preview:
Fictional bundle: maintenance tasks
Owns: task records and task state
Depends on: declared asset query interface
Consumes: asset.updated with declared payload
Optional dependency absent: task history still readable
Acceptance: event replay is idempotent; migration can roll back
marketing.proof_summary: Canonical reference hashes and 106 documentation checks passed. They establish reference coverage, not a deployed framework. Native package availability and app behavior need checking against your installed Torque environment.
marketing.next_step: Bring the host mount plan and one domain you want to add.
marketing.example_note: Fictional worked example. It illustrates the intended output; it is not a measured result or a real customer story.
install_notes: Requires Git and Python 3.11+ for the repository installer. The portable method itself can be read by a compatible agent without a service or provider account.
The destination is a skills-parent folder. Use the discovery path supported by your agent; ~/.agents/skills is an example, not a universal host setting.
Keep the complete installed folder, references and license together. Identical reinstall is safe; conflicts are refused. A deliberate --replace keeps a dated backup.

portable_method.name: build-with-torque
portable_method.contract: Agent Skills directory; caller applies the method; no independent execution loop is installed.

portable.input: Caller task and explicitly authorized context
portable.output: Build a domain that still fits the rest of the application.
portable.failure: Report insufficient evidence, unsupported context or host limitation; never turn discovery into an execution claim.

native.status: Existing declared entrypoints preserved; runtime signatures, service access and installation tests remain separate evidence.

installation.scope: Shared canonical portable installer only; not the legacy repository helper or native package installation.

runtime.status: Host/caller authorizes each operation; installation is not a tool allowlist or standing approval.

secret_names.native_runtime_inventory: See native documentation; no credentials are bundled or inferred.

dataflow.installation: Shared canonical portable installer only (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/): read portable source tracked at the explicit Git pin and copy locally with SHA-256 receipts; no source text is transmitted. Legacy repository helpers copy current working-tree files and do not uniformly enforce Git pins, tracked membership or hash receipts. Native package builds and downloads have separate network, execution and storage flows described in their installation documentation.
dataflow.method: Caller supplies authorized context; existing promise and boundaries govern output.
dataflow.native_runtime: Provider/network/storage flows are owned by native interfaces and host authorization; these files do not enable them.

source_policy.revision: The shared canonical portable installer (https://michaeljabbour.github.io/reports/capability-installer/) requires an explicit full 40-character Git commit and never infers latest. This guarantee does not apply uniformly to legacy or native installers; the legacy repository helper is an operator-controlled working-tree copy without Git-pin, tracked-membership or SHA-256 receipt enforcement.
source_policy.repository_rename: Public identity may change; skill folder, imports, entrypoints, tool IDs and schemas remain stable.
source_policy.research: .research/market remains local and ignored; AGENTS governs refresh.

film.heading: Own your tables. Declare the rest.
film.blurb: In 70 seconds, Pockets the raccoon night porter borrows a master key to fetch another floor’s news, and the tasks floor goes dark when the assets floor renames a column. Build with Torque keeps each domain on its own keycard floor: you ask a neighbour through the coordinator on a declared line, react to past-tense events, plan what still works when a neighbour is gone, and try data changes on a mock-up floor with a way back. Captions are on the player; a transcript is below.
film.note: The hotel and its building-maintenance app are a fictional example. The film shows how the skill behaves; it does not report results.

legacy_repository.documentation: Existing install_commands and repository installation documentation, where provided.
legacy_repository.source_policy: Operator-controlled current working-tree copy. It can include untracked files and can operate outside a Git checkout; no uniform Git pin or SHA-256 transaction receipt is enforced.
legacy_repository.permissions: Review the specific command and destination; shared-installer transaction and permission guarantees do not describe this route.

native.documentation: interfaces.native, runtime_install_commands and project installation documentation, where provided.
native.source_policy: Native packaging, host composition and download routes retain their own version and provenance rules; shared portable receipt guarantees do not automatically apply.
native.permissions: Package builds may execute build tools; dependency or artifact downloads may use the network. Review the documented command, dependencies, destination and runtime authorization separately.
